facts.statement: Aquilarhinus is a genus of hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaur known from the Aguja Formation in Texas, United States.
facts.quote: Aquilarhinus (meaning "eagle snout" after the unusual beak morphology) is a genus of hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaur from the Aguja Formation from Texas in the United States.

facts.statement: The only known species in the genus Aquilarhinus is Aquilarhinus palimentus.
facts.quote: The type and only species is Aquilarhinus palimentus.

facts.statement: Researchers infer that Aquilarhinus possessed a shovel-like beak morphology distinct from other hadrosaurs due to its unusual dentary.
facts.quote: Due to its unusual dentary, it has been inferred to have had shovel-like beak morphology, different from the beaks of other hadrosaurs.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Aquilarhinus was discovered in the Lower Shale of the Aguja Formation within Big Bend National Park, Texas.
facts.quote: The holotype fossil (TMM 42452-1) of Aquilarhinus was discovered in the Lower Shale of the Aguja Formation in Big Bend National Park, Texas.

facts.statement: Most parts of the Aquilarhinus holotype were collected in 1983, with additional elements found during excavations in 1999.
facts.quote: Most parts of the specimen were collected in 1983, but additional elements were collected during continued excavations in 1999.

facts.statement: The species was reclassified into the new genus Aquilarhinus and named Aquilarhinus palimentus in 2019.
facts.quote: In 2019, the species was reclassified into a new genus and given its binomial name Aquilarhinus palimentus.

facts.statement: The specific name palimentus refers to the shovel-like shape of the predentary bone, derived from Latin words for shovel and chin.
facts.quote: The specific epithet palimentus would derive from the Latin words 'pala', meaning shovel, and 'mentus', meaning chin, referring the shape of the predentary and its resemblance to a spade or shovel.

facts.statement: Aquilarhinus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 75 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a final del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 75 millones de años, durante el Campaniense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Aquilarhinus is classified within the family Hadrosauridae.
Aquilarhinus belongs to the superfamily Hadrosauroidea.
Aquilarhinus is part of the infraorder Iguanodontia.
The time range for Aquilarhinus is estimated to be between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The unique rostrum shape of Aquilarhinus is interpreted as an adaptation for shoveling and scooping up vegetation.
facts.quote: The differences in the rostrum were interpreted as being a functional adaptation for "shoveling out and scooping up vegetation."

rejected.statement: Aquilarhinus was first described in 2001 as a new species of the genus Kritosaurus.
rejected.quote: The specimen was first described in 2001 as a new species of Kritosaurus.
